r: **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**; against the **formation of Chirala municipality** (tax Rs 4,000 → 40,000); no-tax from March 1921; Gandhi visited 6 April 1921; on **25 April 1921** 13,572 people left for the camp **Ramnagar**; volunteer corps **Ramadandu**; Duggirala arrested Sept 1921
**Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary** – **"Andhra Shivaji"**; **Shanti Sena**; village officers resigned **so that no land revenue could be collected**
**Kanneganti Hanumanthu** (born Guntur district); **first forest satyagraha in Andhra**; refusal of the **pullari – tax on grazing cattle in the forests**
Failed rains, 1921; pullari **12 annas a cow** (Forest Act 1878)
**Social boycott at Macherla**; **300 cattle impounded at Minchalapadu**
**Hanumanthu shot dead in the cattle rescue at Minchalapadu, 22 Feb 1922**
**Unnava Lakshminarayana** (wrote **Nayakuralu** in jail) and Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari; **Konda Venkatappayya** tried to moderate it

0.x: **Guntur no-tax campaign** suspended on **11 Feb 1922** after Gandhi's message to **Konda Venkatappayya**.
All three struggles were in the old **Guntur** district. **Chirala** is famous for **handloom textiles**.

r: **January 1921**, Vijayawada – set up committees at **district, taluk and village** level
**31 March – 1 April 1921** (venue "Gandhinagar"); leaders **accepted Gandhi's leadership** of the national struggle
Gandhi, Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, the Ali brothers
**Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao** – Gandhi's speech into Telugu
**Pingali Venkayya** (born **Bhatlapenumarru**) presented the **tricolour flag** design (with the **charkha**), accepted by Gandhi; PM paid tribute on his **150th birth anniversary (August 2026)**
Formed the volunteer force **Ramadandu**; **first Andhra leader to be AICC secretary**

1.x: At Kakinada **Durgabai** translated his speech and gave Rs 5,000; women leaders **Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma, Unnava Lakshmibayamma** emerged.

r: Boycotted by Andhra (Justice Party won **63 of 98**); first ministry **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** (17 Dec 1920)
Allowed provinces civil disobedience, incl. no-tax
**National College – Eluru**; Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi – Chirala; Pallepadu Ashram – Nellore; Seethanagaram Ashram near Rajahmundry (now Kasturba Ashram); **Ponduru (Srikakulam) khadi**
**Tanguturi Prakasam**, **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, **Bulusu Sambamurthy** (gave up his practice, 1920), Konda Venkatappayya, Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao
Founded her Home Rule League (Sept 1916; Tilak's 28 April 1916); first woman INC President (**1917**)
**Sarojini Naidu** – first Indian woman president (1925); Nellie Sengupta 1933

Organised the movement and its **branches** in Andhra; **secretary** of the Andhra Home Rule League; **translated Sarojini Naidu's "Awake Mother"** as **"Nutana Haindava Matrugeetamu"**; pamphlet **Swarajya Paramoddesham**
Organised Besant's tour of **Kakinada, Rajahmundry, Eluru** (1916, after Lucknow)
52 branches by 1917; Home Rule flag hoisted at **Coimbatore**
Machilipatnam National College students wore "Besant lockets"; protests at Tenali and Vijayawada called **Confinement Day** protests
Krishna Patrika – Mutnuri Krishna Rao; Desamata – Chilakamarti
**22 Jan 1918** – president **Nyapati Subba Rao**, secretary Konda Venkatappayya
Led by Nyapati (**20 Dec 1917**) for a separate Andhra province
Recommended **Tilak** as delegate to the (Paris) **Peace Conference**
**Viplava Parivarthanam** (play, banned in the Non-Cooperation Movement)
